title: Gas Station
statement: There are n gas stations on a circle. `gas[i]` is the fuel at station i and `cost[i]` is the fuel required to travel to the next station. You start with an empty tank. Return the unique starting station index that completes the circuit, or -1 if none exists.
hints: If the total gas is less than the total cost, no start works.
If the total is sufficient, a start exists. The greedy start is the station after the last time the running tank went negative.
A negative tank means every station in the current segment fails as a start. Reset the tank and try the next station.

approaches.name: Simulate every start
approaches.explanation: Drive the circle from each index.

approaches.name: One pass with a reset
approaches.explanation: Total surplus proves existence. The last reset is the start.

editorial: Let diff[i] = gas[i] - cost[i]. A feasible start has every prefix of the circular walk nonnegative. If the sum of diff is negative, return -1. Otherwise walk once, and whenever the tank drops below zero, the next index is the new candidate and the tank resets. That candidate works because every earlier segment had negative surplus and cannot be part of a feasible prefix.
